topic.title: Why rich people love debt and you're scared of it

title: You borrow for a car. The rich borrow for this 🤫
description:
Why do the rich love debt while you're scared of it?
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Car loan or growth loan: which one do you have? Comment

lines.text: You're scared of debt. I love it. Let me show you why.
Same bank, two loans. Rohan borrows $40,000, I borrow $100,000, and one question decides who gets richer.
Mine buys a shiny new car! Just 7% a year, paid over 60 months. Easy.
But a car loses value every year you drive it. So Rohan pays $7,523 in interest for something that keeps shrinking.
My loan costs 6% a year. Over 10 years, that's $33,225 in interest, even more than Rohan pays.
The difference is what I buy with it: a building, or a business that can grow.
If it grows an assumed 8% a year, in 10 years it gains $115,892.
Hold on. You still pay the bank all that interest!
Gladly. The interest is my cost, the growth is my profit. Good debt buys something that earns more than the loan costs.
That's why the rich love debt: the car shrinks, the building grows. But if what they buy stops growing, the loan still has to be paid.
So I'm not scared of debt. I'm scared of my car loan. And honestly, Sharma...
